Solve a system of nonlinear equations

Source: R/optimlib.R
optimlib_root.Rd

Finds par such that fn(par) = 0 using Broyden's method, a quasi-Newton root finder.

Usage

optimlib_root(
  par,
  fn,
  jac = NULL,
  ...,
  method = c("broyden", "broyden_df"),
  control = list()
)

Arguments

par

Numeric vector of starting values.

fn

Function called as fn(par, ...) and returning a numeric vector of the same length as par.

jac

Optional Jacobian of fn, called as jac(par, ...) and returning a square matrix. If NULL, OptimLib builds its own approximation.

...

Further arguments passed to fn and jac.

method

"broyden" (Broyden's method) or "broyden_df" (derivative-free variant of Li and Fukushima, 2000, with a nonmonotone line search). Without jac, both start from an identity approximation of the Jacobian and can diverge from poor starting values; supplying jac or a better par helps. Check success and fn_values.

control

A list of settings, or the result of optimlib_control().

Value

A list with elements par, fn_values (fn at par), success, iterations, error and method.

Examples

# x^2 + y^2 = 4 and x = y
optimlib_root(c(1, 0.5), function(x) c(x[1]^2 + x[2]^2 - 4, x[1] - x[2]))
#> $par
#> [1] 1.414214 1.414214
#> 
#> $fn_values
#> [1] -8.881784e-16  0.000000e+00
#> 
#> $success
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
#> $iterations
#> [1] 18
#> 
#> $error
#> [1] 1.776357e-10
#> 
#> $method
#> [1] "broyden"
#>
